title: Tunisian reverse stitch tablet case
excerpt: A padded tablet sleeve worked in DK yarn using Tunisian reverse stitch. The reverse stitch creates a textured ribbed fabric that gives a secure fit.
sourceNotes: Tunisian reverse stitch inserts the hook through the back vertical bar rather than the front, creating a raised ridge on the right side that adds structure to the fabric.

glossaryTerms.definition: Worked by inserting the hook through the back vertical bar of the previous row, drawing up a loop. Produces a purl-like ridge on the right side.
A simple seaming stitch worked by passing the needle over the edge of both fabric layers and through, repeating evenly along the length to join them.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 sts x 14 rows = 10 cm in Tunisian reverse stitch on 4.0 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 20 cm wide x 26 cm deep , fits most standard tablets.

Chain 38. Row 1 forward pass: pick up a loop in each chain (38 loops). Return pass. From row 2: forward pass , insert hook through back vertical bar of each stitch, draw up a loop; repeat across. Return pass as row 1. Work until each panel measures 26 cm. Bind off.
Hold panels with right sides out. Using the tapestry needle, work whip stitch along both side edges and across the bottom. Leave the top open. Weave in all ends.
